community_roundup.title: COMMUNITY ROUNDUP: active UAP discussion, no new verifiable development identified
community_roundup.lede: The scan found no new verifiable UAP development to add to the desk. The accessible r/UFOs feed was active with discussion of Jay Stratton, a viral Grusch interview, a reported Israel-border object, sighting submissions, and historical cases. Public X search returned the logged-out application shell rather than attributable post text; the other requested Reddit feeds returned rate-limit responses. Community attention is recorded as signal, not evidence.

sections.heading: MOST IMPORTANT TO DISCLOSURE: a reported lead, not a breakthrough
sections.body: The strongest public lead still on the desk is the New York Post's October 10 report that Rep. Eric Burlison said he would explore whether intelligence-community witnesses connected to a late-2025 orange-orb encounter could testify before Congress. That is a reported possibility, not an announced hearing, subpoena, or public witness appearance. This edition found no new primary record changing that status. Reddit discussion of Jay Stratton is a community lead, not confirmation of a new interview, release, or finding.

sections.heading: TRENDING / LOUDEST: attention cannot be measured cleanly this morning
sections.body: The accessible r/UFOs RSS feed returned 20 active threads. Visible titles included a Jay Stratton television segment, a claim about a NASA astronaut's religious interpretation, a weekly UAP roundup, new sighting submissions from Ohio, Israel, Florida, Massachusetts, and California, a Coyne Incident recreation, launch-identification chatter, the latest Grusch/Joe Rogan discussion, and older document and photograph threads. No thread establishes its underlying claim. The other four requested Reddit feeds returned HTTP 429, while logged-out X exposed only its application shell rather than attributable posts. The desk therefore records no X account as having posted.

sections.heading: FUN / INTERESTING: the archive remains a map of the argument
sections.body: The most useful community leads were the Jay Stratton broadcast discussion, the Coyne Incident technical recreation, the Israel-border report, and a document-forensics thread about pre-Roswell material. They are leads and historical discussion, not independently authenticated developments. The Coyne material may suit a future archive piece if the original flight records, testimony, and technical reconstruction can be separated rather than poured into one heroic story.

community_roundup.editorial_note: COMMUNITY ROUNDUP: This is a map of public discussion and accessible community media, not verified news. The New York Post and Ask a Pol items are labeled REPORTED because the publications and attributed statements are verifiable while their implications require further checking. Reddit threads and creator material are community leads only. Public X search exposed no attributable post text in this run; four requested Reddit feeds returned HTTP 429. Those limitations are recorded as limitations, not silence.

items.headline: AARO public record: cases, reports, and official releases
items.summary: The All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office is the U.S. Department of Defense office assigned to receive and investigate reports of unidentified anomalous phenomena. This is a monitored source page; it is not evidence that a new case was announced today.

items.headline: NASA UAP research and public material
items.summary: NASA's UAP material explains its scientific data and research posture. It is useful for tracking what the agency has actually published, while keeping scientific interpretation separate from internet speculation.

items.headline: NASA news releases: check before calling a development news
items.summary: A daily newsroom check begins with the agency's own releases and public statements. No headline is promoted here unless the underlying release, document, or named source can be read and linked.

items.headline: Defense Department releases and statements
items.summary: The Defense Department release archive is a first stop for official claims about military policy, investigations, and records. Official wording will be labeled as an official claim rather than silently converted into an independently verified fact.

items.headline: Rep. James Comer says a UAP hearing may return during the November lame-duck period
items.summary: Ask a Pol UAP published an interview in which House Oversight Chair James Comer said the committee might try to pick up a UAP hearing during an ‘aggressive’ post-election lame-duck period. The report establishes an attributed public statement, not an announced hearing, date, topic, or witness list; no committee notice was independently verified in this scan.

This verifies the publication and its attributed framing, not the underlying account, the 17-day duration, the aircraft identification, or any official finding.

items.headline: New York Post reports Rep. Eric Burlison may explore testimony from witnesses to a late-2025 orange-orb account
items.summary: The New York Post reported on October 10, 2026 that Rep. Eric Burlison said he would explore whether intelligence-community witnesses connected to a late-2025 orange-orb encounter could testify before Congress. The report says some witnesses have met lawmakers privately and have not shared all alleged footage. This verifies the publication and attributed statement, not an announced hearing, the witnesses’ identities, the encounter’s interpretation, or the authenticity and completeness of the evidence. The report points to an underlying government-released first-person narrative that should be read separately.
